REJUGÉE le 2026-09-03 après ldpy 0.6.3 (fiche ldpy/027). Elle était classée not-expressible : les 19 Namespace sont tous passés PAR VALEUR à g.bind() et exportés par global, ce que @prefix — purement lexical — ne pouvait pas faire. Les deux changements de 0.6.3 la débloquent entièrement. (1) 'as EX' lie l'objet Namespace à un nom Python, et 'global @prefix ... as EX .' l'exporte : les 19 global survivent. (2) un graphe DÉSIGNÉ hérite des préfixes du bloc, donc les 19 lignes g.bind() disparaissent purement et simplement — c'est le gain principal, 19 lignes d'échafaudage contre 0. Le pilote a dû être refait : il comparait le graphe rendu, dont les triplets viennent du helper et ne dépendent d'aucun préfixe — il restait vert sur une traduction cassée. Un demo() identique des deux côtés rend maintenant les liaisons du graphe, les globals exportés et les triplets. Casse délibérée vérifiée : FAIL puis OK après restauration.

[note antérieure] context_shim.py restores `from .graph_common import add_common_elements` (a relative import needing a real parent package) with a near-verbatim copy of arborist/graph_common.py's `add_common_elements` and `CommonNamespaces`/`NS`; `__version__` is inlined as the literal from arborist/__init__.py (VERSION = (0, 5)). One compatibility fix unrelated to the region: the shim declares `DC = Namespace("http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/")` instead of importing `rdflib.namespace.DC`, because on the pinned rdflib 7.2.1 that DC is a `DefinedNamespace` restricted to the 15 Dublin Core Elements terms and raises on `DC.modified` (a DCTERMS term) -- the source repository plainly ran against an rdflib where this was not enforced. Same IRI, same resulting URIRef, no triple changes. NOT-EXPRESSIBLE, decisively so from evidence inside the region itself (not a downstream guess): all 19 `Namespace(...)` objects (BONT, BRDFFO, ..., PROV) are, without exception, passed BY VALUE to `g.bind(prefix, NS)` a few lines later (`g.bind("bont", BONT)`, ..., `g.bind("prov", PROV)`) -- rdflib's `NamespaceManager.bind` needs an actual runtime object, and `@prefix` is a lexical, transpile-time binding table entry with `no run-time object` (INSTRUCTIONS.md 1). Every one of the 19 is also re-exported via the `global` statement at the top of the function, for use elsewhere in extract_emissions.py -- a second, independent reason the object must survive the block. This is exactly the documented case in ldpy/docs/how-to/migrate-from-rdflib.md, section 'What not to rewrite': 'A Namespace as an object: @prefix is a lexical declaration, not a value. If you need to pass a namespace around, keep the Namespace constant.' Unlike two out of three regions in the prior ns_def_local batch, there is no partial win here: every single Namespace in this function is bound onto the graph as an object, so none of the 19 can be swapped for a lexical @prefix without breaking the very next line that uses it. translated.ldpy substitutes all 19 `NS = Namespace(IRI)` assignments with `@prefix ns: <IRI> .` and leaves the rest of the function (the `global` statement, the `.format(BRDFTIME, ...)` construction, all 19 `g.bind()` calls) untouched, so `rdfeval check` reproduces the failure concretely rather than asserting it: `NameError: name 'BRDFTIME' is not defined` at `extent2011node = URIRef("{}{}".format(BRDFTIME, '2011'))` (line 38) -- the first read of a substituted name, before even reaching the `g.bind()` calls that would fail the same way. `def f(): @prefix ns: <IRI> .` inside a function, then any later use of `NS`/`ns` as a Python object (`g.bind("ns", NS)`, or reading it back after `global NS`), is the minimal extract. The ldpy LSP's own diagnostics on the substituted file independently confirm this: `global BONT` (etc., all 19) is flagged `unused: name is never assigned in scope`, because `@prefix` defines no Python name at all. extent2011node itself, taken alone, WOULD be directly expressible -- it only produces a URIRef that then travels as an ordinary variable (also `global`, but that is fine for a plain term, only Namespace objects are the problem): `brdftime:2011` (a prefixed name) is the more specific construction for `URIRef("{}{}".format(BRDFTIME, '2011'))`. It is not used here because BRDFTIME still has to exist as a `Namespace` object four lines later for `g.bind("brdftime", BRDFTIME)`; keeping both a `@prefix` and a `Namespace(...)` for the same IRI would not be a translation, just added machinery beside the untouched original -- so the whole namespace-declaration idiom stays classified together as not-expressible rather than split into 18 not-expressible plus 1 directly-expressible. translation_status stays draft and cannot go final: there is no notation that covers a Namespace exported as an object (by `global`, and independently by `g.bind()`) without changing extract_emissions.py's own contract with the rest of the module.
